1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Felsheim for three days. Anna Weber's older sister had left for Berlin in the spring, and since then, Anna had been running the village's small pharmacy on her own.
As darkness fell, she closed the shutters, counted the day's earnings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lied down when there was a loud knocking at the door downstairs. A man's voice called out, "Is anyone there?"
Standing at the door was a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloody cloth. He introduced himself as Konrad Wolf and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need a bandage," Wolf said softly. "I can pay. Is three thousand five hundred marks enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oilskin from his jacket. "This letter must reach the Steinbach monastery before May eighteenth."
Anna must have been blind; only now did she notice how pale he was.
Still, she refused his money and simply said, "I'll take you into the mountains tomorrow morning."
2: They set off at dawn. Anna carried a basket on her back containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up, they encountered old Hans Becker, who was chopping wood. He set his axe aside and said softly that three strangers had come to the village entrance yesterday evening, asking about an injured young man.
"Take the path, Anna," Hans Becker said. "The main road isn't safe." Anna thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Anna led the way, placing each step with care. Wolf followed her in silence.
Around noon the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and the roof of Steinbach Monastery appeared in the distance. At the gate stood a nun, Sister Hildegard, who received the guests at the monastery.
Sister Hildegard took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The Abbess has been waiting two years for this letter."
Wolf said to Anna, "I owe you my life." Anna smiled. "Then next time, you can repair the roof of my pharmacy." Wolf stayed at the monastery.
In the evening, Anna descended the mountain alone. By the time she arrived home, it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat behind the shop counter for a long time.
